description: Which harness each Toolkit hook belongs to, the hard rules it enforces and why it runs on each event; which shared modules are neutral policy or library code; and the mixing that existed when the rule landed (known_open, which only shrinks). Rule: repo/docs/agent-playbooks/hook-design.md, Harness-specific by default. Checked in this repository's CI by repo/scripts/check-hook-scope.cjs.

hard_rules.rule: No merge without the owner's approval; merge text and closure checks.
No push to the default branch, no force push, no raw evidence-store push, no credential in a push or pull request.
Closing words only when UAT allows them.
Agents never answer owner-only questions and never edit Toolkit user state.
Coding gate sessions keep their route and stamp their verdicts.
Helpers in gate runs are admitted on their route, one layer deep, and every subagent names a model or helper.

hooks.reason: Updater, sync and install health for this computer: not a hard rule. Its hook-mode output is Claude Code's.

events.SessionStart: Session start: a newer Toolkit is found and synced here, before later chats load their hooks (hooks load before this runs, so no event helps the current chat).
Session start: this chat needs governance on or off, the governed rules and (in the desktop app) how to ask the owner before its first step, and again after compaction erases them.
events.UserPromptSubmit: Turn start: only the owner's own message carries a merge approval or a governance answer.
events.PreToolUse: Before the tool runs: a merge, push, closure, owner-only answer, user-state edit or off-route gate write is refused before it happens.
events.PostToolUse: Right after AskUserQuestion returns: the owner's tap on a Toolkit card is recorded from that card's own answer.

events.PreToolUse: Before an Agent or Task launch: a gate helper off its route, a second layer or a launch naming no model is refused before it starts.
Before a Bash or PowerShell call runs: AI attribution, a force push, a raw evidence-store push or a credential is stopped before the commit or push leaves.

hooks.reason: Gate custody journal and programme refresh mark: a records job, not a hard rule.

events.PostToolUse: Right after a shell or GitHub connector call: marks that this turn wrote to GitHub, from that call's own result.
events.Stop: Turn end: the gate checkpoint journal and the programme refresh start can wait until the agent stops.

hooks.reason: Cleans the cloud footer Claude Code adds to GitHub text; no other harness adds it.

events.PostToolUse: Right after a shell or GitHub connector write returns: the footer GitHub sent back is cleaned from that write's own result.

hooks.reason: The controller's turn-end nudge for owed findings, gate records and finished side sessions, and one line per chat to the owner while Toolkit permission lines are out of date: records and reminders, not hard rules.

events.Stop: Turn end: owed work is only certain once the agent stops, and a nudge then still reaches the controller before the owner's next turn; the permissions line waits for the end of the chat's first turn, so it never holds a tool call.

hooks.reason: Keeps the env edit file's real key values out of the chat by refusing Claude Code tool calls on that folder. No hard rule on the closed list covers reading it, so making it one for every harness is an owner decision.

events.PreToolUse: Before a file or shell tool runs: a read, search or listing of the env edit folder would put every key value in the chat, so it is refused before it happens.
Before a start_session call runs: a gate brief missing its Gate, Route or Assignment line, or a launch off the route's model and effort, is refused before the session starts.
events.PostToolUse: Right after a gate start returns: the next steps (effort raise, assignment record, wake) need that call's own session id.

hooks.reason: Codex's session start: runs the updater in-process and prints Codex's plain-text governance and catch-up lines.

events.SessionStart: Session start: the update check and the governance on or off lines are needed before this chat's first step.

events.UserPromptSubmit: Turn start: only the owner's own message carries a merge approval or a governance answer.
events.PreToolUse: Before the tool runs: a merge, push, closure, owner-only answer, user-state edit or off-route helper launch is refused before it happens.

hooks.reason: Gate custody journal and programme refresh mark: a records job, not a hard rule.

events.PostToolUse: Right after a shell or GitHub connector call: marks that this turn wrote to GitHub, from that call's own result.
events.Stop: Turn end: the gate checkpoint journal and the programme refresh start can wait until the agent stops.

modules.reason: The merge hold and the cloud merge-card taps it reads.
Owner-only answers, user-state edits and the governance question.
Closing references and UAT before a close.
Force push, evidence-store push and credential checks, and the credential formats they scan for.
Helper launch admission: the shared adapter core, its per-harness lanes, the helper specification and the gate contract it compiles.
Reads a shell call or a typed command into plain words for the policy modules.
Workflow YAML reader; `shell` here is the workflow step key, not a tool.

not_vocabulary.shell: The `shell` key of a workflow step, not a tool name.

modules.reason: Governance state, binding, answers and repository-settings reads, the same for every harness.
Programme state; `Agent` is the word in an "Agent UAT owed" line.

not_vocabulary.Agent: The word in the "Agent UAT owed" line, not a tool name.

modules.reason: Programme records, checkpoints, refresh marks and decision traces, the same for every harness.
Toolkit plumbing: version, paths, user state, update markers, managed blocks, and permission blocks.
Reads a session transcript's first lines; its Claude Code reading moves to the Claude dialect in #1474 S2 (the vocabulary check cannot see a transcript format).
The daily slow-CI record and its line, the same for every harness; each hook decides where the line goes.
Finds and starts the Claude CLI for setup and review runs; no hook decision reads it.
Installers of the vendored plain-text and personal-data checks, read to compare a governed copy with its source.

boundaries.reason: The updater: it keeps this computer's Toolkit, plugins and rules current for every harness, so its setup modules are harness-specific setup code, not hook decisions. Its own hook output is the two-harnesses item below until #1474 S5 gives Claude its own session-start entry over it.

dynamic_requires.reason: Renders with the same file from the source checkout the copies are pinned to.
The plain-text check installer from the given Toolkit root.
Each worker thread runs refreshMergedBinding from the module it is given: the governance state module (tests pass a stand-in).
